purpose: Record independent fresh-review verdicts for prepared Human Infra card-promotion packs while keeping model admission and individual-use claims blocked.

scope.reviewedBatchLabel: 统计、生存分析、目标试验与预测模型方法锚点
scope.artifactPromotionDecision: FRB-01 rows may proceed to bounded artifact filling; model admission remains blocked until card filling, downgrade checks and model gates pass.
nonClaims: This register is not a completed Source Card set, variable-card set, endpoint-card set, uncertainty-card set, transfer-boundary-card set or downgrade-check set.
This register does not authorize calibrated prediction, individual recommendation, individual death-date output, intervention ranking, domain-claim upgrade or clinical-validity claims.
This register completes only the first independent fresh-review batch; the remaining prepared packs still require fresh review.

freshReviewEvidence.finding: HERO metadata identifies the source as a 1958 Journal of the American Statistical Association journal article by Kaplan and Meier, volume 53 issue 282, pages 457-481. The abstract describes incomplete observations, loss/censoring-like events, independence assumptions that require scrutiny, and nonparametric estimation of P(t).
The paper defines the survival function P(t) and product-limit estimate, and discusses losses, observation limits, and dependence between lifetimes and loss times.

registeredExactClaimUses: Supports aggregate time-to-event accounting for a defined risk set when time zero, event definition and censoring status are explicit.
registeredTransferBoundaries: Transfer only as survival-curve and event-time vocabulary. It does not validate domain parameters, prove intervention benefit, or authorize personal prognosis.
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.exactClaimUseVerdict: supports aggregate survival-function and event-time accounting only when time zero, event definition, risk set and censoring or loss status are explicit
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.domainTransferVerdict: bounded-transfer-to-survival-curve vocabulary; no intervention benefit, route feasibility, personal prognosis or parameter validation
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.modelPositionVerdict: method-language-only; calibrated prediction and individual prognosis remain blocked
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.uncertaintyBoundaryVerdict: must carry censoring/loss mechanism, time-origin, event-definition and risk-set applicability limits
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.downgradeVerdict: no downgrade required for method vocabulary; downgrade required if used as causal, feasibility or personal-prediction evidence
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.blockedUseVerdict: all protocol blocked uses remain blocked for this batch
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.reviewerNote: Fresh review confirms this source is usable as survival-analysis vocabulary for incomplete observations, not as Human Infra model calibration evidence.

freshReviewEvidence.finding: The publisher page identifies the paper as Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B, volume 34 issue 2, pages 187-202, and summarizes censored failure-time analysis where the hazard function is modeled as explanatory variables and coefficients multiplied by an arbitrary time function.
EPA HERO metadata records the 1972 journal article, page range 187-220, peer review status, and an abstract matching censored failure-time, explanatory-variable and hazard-function language.

registeredExactClaimUses: Supports expressing domain variables as covariates associated with event hazard when time origin, event outcome and covariate measurement are explicit.
registeredTransferBoundaries: Transfer only as hazard vocabulary and covariate-risk positioning. It does not prove causality, personalize risk, or rank interventions by itself.
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.exactClaimUseVerdict: supports expressing explicitly measured covariates as associated with event hazard under a defined time origin and event outcome
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.domainTransferVerdict: bounded-transfer-to-hazard/covariate-risk vocabulary; no causality, personalization, intervention ranking or deployment validity
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.modelPositionVerdict: method-language-only; calibrated prediction, causal inference and individual risk advice remain blocked
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.uncertaintyBoundaryVerdict: must carry proportional-hazard/functional-form, covariate-measurement, censoring, validation and calibration limits
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.downgradeVerdict: no downgrade required for hazard vocabulary; downgrade required if treated as causal effect, calibrated predictor or intervention-ranking evidence
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.blockedUseVerdict: all protocol blocked uses remain blocked for this batch
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.reviewerNote: Fresh review confirms this source supports hazard-model vocabulary and covariate-risk positioning only within explicit modeling assumptions.

sourceAnchorFreshReviews.reviewedSourceTitle: Target Trial Emulation: A Framework for Causal Inference From Observational Data
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.reviewedSourceAuthors: Miguel A. Hernán; Wei Wang; David E. Leaf

freshReviewEvidence.finding: PubMed identifies the JAMA 2022 article, DOI 10.1001/jama.2022.21383, and summarizes target trial emulation as designing an observational study to preserve advantages of a randomized clinical trial while pointing out method limitations.

registeredExactClaimUses: Supports translating a domain intervention question into target-trial fields: eligibility, strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcome, causal contrast and analysis plan.
registeredTransferBoundaries: Transfer only as causal-design discipline for future intervention evaluation. It does not establish that any domain intervention works.
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.exactClaimUseVerdict: supports translating intervention questions into target-trial protocol fields; it does not make observational data causal by label alone
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.domainTransferVerdict: bounded-transfer-to-causal-design discipline; no proof that any Human Infra intervention works and no individual recommendation
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.modelPositionVerdict: causal-design-language-only; effect claims remain blocked until data, assumptions, bias checks and sensitivity analyses pass
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.uncertaintyBoundaryVerdict: must carry eligibility, strategies, assignment, time zero, follow-up, outcome, causal contrast, confounding and transportability limits
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.downgradeVerdict: no downgrade required for causal-design scaffolding; downgrade required for any asserted effect without target-trial-compatible evidence
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.blockedUseVerdict: all protocol blocked uses remain blocked for this batch
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.reviewerNote: Fresh review confirms this source is a design protocol anchor, not an evidence shortcut for intervention benefit.

sourceAnchorFreshReviews.reviewedSourceTitle: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods

freshReviewEvidence.finding: PubMed identifies the BMJ 2024 TRIPOD+AI article, PMID 38626948, DOI 10.1136/bmj-2023-078378, and states the guideline aims at complete, accurate and transparent reporting of prediction-model studies.
EQUATOR lists TRIPOD+AI as guidance for reporting studies that develop a prediction model or evaluate performance and links checklist materials.

registeredExactClaimUses: Supports reporting requirements for prediction models: data source, participants, predictors, outcome, model development, validation, calibration and limitations.
registeredTransferBoundaries: Transfer only as a prediction-reporting and validation checklist. It does not authorize clinical prediction, individual advice or automated action.
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.exactClaimUseVerdict: supports reporting requirements for prediction-model development and performance evaluation, including AI and regression models
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.domainTransferVerdict: bounded-transfer-to-reporting/checklist vocabulary; no clinical validity, deployment fitness, calibration proof or individual advice
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.modelPositionVerdict: reporting-guideline-only; Human Infra toy models remain non-clinical until validation, calibration and bias assessment are independently evidenced
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.uncertaintyBoundaryVerdict: must carry data-source, participant, predictor, outcome, validation, calibration, limitation and transparency reporting limits
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.downgradeVerdict: no downgrade required for reporting-standard use; downgrade required if used as model-performance evidence
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.blockedUseVerdict: all protocol blocked uses remain blocked for this batch
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.reviewerNote: Fresh review confirms TRIPOD+AI is a reporting and transparency anchor, not proof that any Human Infra model works.

sourceAnchorFreshReviews.reviewedSourceTitle: What Cancer Screening Statistics Really Tell Us

freshReviewEvidence.finding: NCI explains why screening statistics require careful interpretation, including survival-after-diagnosis versus mortality endpoints.
NCI provides official context for cancer screening research and screening-benefit boundaries.

registeredExactClaimUses: Supports separating earlier detection, survival-after-diagnosis statistics, mortality reduction, overdiagnosis, follow-up burden and net screening benefit.
registeredTransferBoundaries: Transfer only as screening endpoint and bias vocabulary. It does not endorse or reject individual screening and does not prove mortality benefit.
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.exactClaimUseVerdict: supports separating earlier detection, survival-after-diagnosis statistics, mortality reduction, overdiagnosis, follow-up burden and net benefit
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.domainTransferVerdict: bounded-transfer-to-screening endpoint and bias vocabulary; no endorsement or rejection of individual screening
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.modelPositionVerdict: boundary-language-only; screening benefit, harm and mortality claims require population/test/follow-up/mortality endpoint cards
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.uncertaintyBoundaryVerdict: must carry lead-time, length bias, overdiagnosis, false-positive, follow-up-burden and mortality-endpoint limits
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.downgradeVerdict: bounded support only; downgrade any row that treats earlier diagnosis or survival-after-diagnosis as mortality-benefit proof
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.blockedUseVerdict: all protocol blocked uses remain blocked for this batch
sourceAnchorFreshReviews.reviewerNote: Fresh review confirms NCI material is suitable for screening-bias guardrails, not for individual screening advice or mortality-benefit proof.
